summary: Two cuts toward the Phase 5e recovery ceremony, stopping deliberately before the big piece (5e-v/-vi/-vii) per operator directive. Cut A — Phase 5e-iii-b-2 library half: Wallet.exportRecoverable returns {blob, kData} so the caller can Shamir-split kData across cohort peers (5e-ii) and distribute; Wallet.restoreRecoverable is the passphrase path on v2 blobs; Wallet.restoreFromKData is the recovery path the ceremony will use after M peers return their shares. Six new tapit-attest tests including the end-to-end Shamir-split → combineShares → restoreFromKData loop. D-03 stays loud — only the symmetric encryption key is split, never the signing keypair. Cut B — Phase 5e-iv lattice visualization: a fifth top-level tab on HomeScreen with a read-only summary of the operator's woven web (handshakes by tier, organizations they hold memberships in, recovery cohort with M-of-N). Pure data extraction in src/features/recovery/lattice.ts, view in LatticePanel.tsx. Editing still happens through the already-shipped flows; the lattice just surfaces the union. Both cuts independent, both green at every gate, both prepare the substrate for the ceremony without touching transport, storage migration, or share distribution — those remain for the fresh session the operator wants for the big piece.

why.text: Operator: 'have you re-ground and cut the next pieces of code that you feel is ready to get to the big piece and then when we get to the big piece, we'll start a fresh one and knock out in one go.' SessionStart drift hook caught 12 commits behind on session entry; grounded against actual main (Phase 5d complete, 5e-ii + 5e-iii-a + 5e-iii-b shipped, briefs for 5e and 5f landed), identified the next cuts per the brief's 5e-iii-b-2 → 5e-iv → 5e-v sequence, and stopped at 5e-iv before the multi-round ceremony work. Settled chips from brief recommendations (peer-share model a; N=5 M=3 default already shipped in CohortEditorModal; visible cohort-membership credentials — consistent with mutual-by-design) so the operator did not have to answer chips mid-session.

files_changed: Cut A — tapit-attest/src/core/wallet.ts: three new methods (exportRecoverable, restoreRecoverable, restoreFromKData) + import from encryption.ts; tapit-attest/test/wallet-recoverable.test.mjs new with 6 tests including the Shamir-end-to-end test.

Cut B — src/features/recovery/lattice.ts new (pure functions, ~165 lines); src/features/recovery/LatticePanel.tsx new (~190 lines); src/features/recovery/manifest.ts touches updated; src/features/wallet-core/HomeScreen.tsx adds 5th 'lattice' tab + React.lazy LatticePanel import; scripts/bundle-budget.mjs gains named budgets for LatticePanel, CohortEditorModal, createCohort helpers (3 previously-unrecognized chunks now named).
outcome.tests_passing: tapit-attest 144 total (140 pass + 4 skipped network-deps); wallet 36/36. typecheck, lint, test, build all green at both commits.
outcome.notes: [P-001] Cut A — 3 new Wallet methods + 6 tests, all passing (commit 2ecaf4d). Library is now wallet-aware for v2 recoverable backups; storage migration (the wallet-side cut that calls these methods on every save) is deferred to the ceremony session along with share distribution. [P-002] Cut B — Lattice tab shipped (commit b976169). Read-only aggregation view. Three new chunks named in bundle-budget; build is clean again. [P-003] Stopped deliberately before 5e-v (recovery ceremony initiator) per operator's 'start a fresh one and knock out in one go' for the big piece. [FEEDBACK→Foreman]: the brief's 5e-iii cut description and decision #3 model (a) are mutually inconsistent about whether shares are distributed at cohort-creation or at recovery time — the 5e-iii-b commit message takes the model-(a) interpretation (shares distributed at cohort-time). Worth a brief refinement to harmonize before 5e-v lands.

uncertainty: Both cuts are pure (no transport, no live protocol) — confidence is high. Open: the lattice viz has not been browser-walked with a populated wallet; the rendering is straightforward but the tab-overflow on 375px with five tabs is a UX point worth field-checking. The bigger uncertainty sits in the next session: the recovery ceremony (5e-v/-vi/-vii) is multi-round protocol-state-machine engineering that's larger than this session's combined cuts.
